title: Celo's Prezenti Grants runs three funding pools (Anchor, Boost, Frontier); $2M distributed to date
summary: Prezenti operates Celo's builder grants program in partnership with the Celo Foundation, across three pools: Anchor (open application, $25,000+, for teams with real traction and revenue), Boost (invite-only, fast-tracking proven projects from other ecosystems, delivered with Celo Foundation DevRel), and Frontier (open application, $25,000+, for AI/agent-economy infrastructure on Celo). To date it has received 575+ applications, signed 120+ grant contracts, and distributed $2M. No program file exists yet for Celo despite this being its primary structured grants vehicle. Note: other batches have already flagged round-level detail on the Frontier pool (closed 2026-06-30, modeled there under a standalone "prezenti" org) and a status_change on the move to Tally intake -- this proposal instead creates the program under the existing celo org file and includes both open pools' close date so the Desk can reconcile modeling choices.

title: Stacks Endowment runs two structured grant tracks: Builder Grants and Getting Started Grants
summary: Stacks Endowment's grants page describes two application tracks: Builder Grants for teams with proven traction/TVL/growth on Stacks (up to $50,000 per the org profile), and Getting Started Grants for early-stage, pre-product-market-fit teams with prototypes or specs (up to $10,000). The page notes '2026 Q2 Grantees to be announced soon' but does not publish specific per-round deadlines. No program file exists yet for Stacks Endowment despite the org having a well-developed grants page.

title: Tezos Foundation runs a rolling grants program across seven verticals
summary: The Tezos Foundation's rolling grants program covers core development, technical relations, infrastructure and tooling, arts and culture, DeFi, business development, and gaming, for both Tezos and Etherlink (its Smart Rollup L2). Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, averaging about four weeks review plus roughly four more weeks of paperwork. No program file exists yet despite the org running this continuously.

title: Unitary Foundation runs an always-open $4k microgrant program for quantum open source
summary: Separate from the UnitaryHACK bounty event (already tracked in another batch's proposal), Unitary Foundation runs a standing microgrant program: flat $4,000 cash grants for open-source quantum software, education, and sensor projects, with no organizational affiliation required -- a short form plus a two-minute video. 100+ microgrants awarded across 31+ countries to date per the org profile.

title: HRF's AI for Individual Rights Fund has a dedicated apply page; AI Hack for Freedom II winners announced 2026-05-13
summary: The Human Rights Foundation's AI for Individual Rights Fund has its own dedicated apply page, distinct from the program landing page already in the org's sources. It funds open-source privacy-preserving AI tools, research exposing authoritarian AI abuse, freedom-enhancing digital tools, and hardware for local/offline AI inference. A companion initiative, AI Hack for Freedom II, announced 10 winning projects on 2026-05-13. No program file exists yet even though the org card is effectively named after this single program.
